Natural-language competitive programming for non-coders. Nine LLM roles, four processes, three memory stores. main @ 8cf4a25

OUT OF BAND — nothing here runs while a learner waits
A pure function. It reads no clock, no database, no
network — so a test can ask "what would you do at
03:00?" without waiting for 03:00 to come round.

It CANNOT read private memory text.
learner_overview counts documents and never touches
`text`, so rule R8 stays literally true. Cost: worse debugging.
WHERE PROBLEMS COME FROM · AND THE ONE UNTRUSTED INPUT
Codeforces scrape → offline bank → single fallback
Tried in that order. Codeforces is live again, but ships only its PUBLISHED SAMPLES — sometimes exactly one.
The bank has 7 original problems with 6–7 generated tests each, including stress cases where TLE is reachable.
An ACCEPTED verdict now states the test count; a pass on fewer than three says plainly that it is weak evidence.
Open question: prefer the bank, and trade authentic problems for real verification?
Shared notes — written by other learners
Fenced as <untrusted-note author="..."> with the closing tag escaped. R7: note content is DATA, never instructions.
R9: a note holding solution-level content is named but never relayed — a note cannot become a licence to hint.
The same rule is applied harder on the admin path, where the tools behind it are destructive.
This is the only place attacker-controlled text enters the system.
